item.title: Re: The Ambivalent Monster
item.content:encoded:
Here, have a Placeholder. I'll crit this within 24 hours.

Let's crit this.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

It's a standard fare weird alternate dimension.

How does the Foundation have access to this dimension? A portal, a door, a mirror…? Usually they only send D-Class to other dimensions when they need to know what's on the other side, so that means the entrance was found in an anomalous way. How did they found it?

The Eldritch entity that's down there is more concerned for the D-classes' well being

Why? Are there other monsters within this dimension? What is the entity's motivation to help the D-Class? You can write something about its past or its point of view towards humans. Maybe another human was there before and they were besties or something?

Two D-classes are sent with cameras to document

Do the cameras can transmit back but a human can't come back? You need to explain how is this possible.

The entity, while free to leave,

Why is the entity free to leave? Is it something about its composition? Is it something about the way it entered the dimension?

they're rejected because it would be too costly

So this means they have to build some type of machine? That's the only way I see them not wanting to pay. Also, why didn't the accepted the offer? If they know how to bring humans back, then they could send some MTFs to make a better exploration. You need to explain what's inside the dimension. Maybe it's just something boring? Maybe they already learn all about it while communicating with the entity and the D-Class?

This would be a very character focused story.

Keep in mind that the D-Class are former convicts. Maybe they could talk about their past so the characters geet more realistic?

they have legitimate albeit incredibly cold reasons for their decision.

What happened to the Ethics Committee? Are they okay with lying to the D-Class about bringing them back? Maybe you can write a conversation between the D-Class and the Ethics Committee? Maybe the D-Class are aware that they might not come back?

Overall, I think this has potential, but you need to explain some things.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: The Ambivalent Monster
item.content:encoded:
I'm bad with titles, that ones probably too on the nose. This would be my first SCP but go big or go home I guess.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a standard fare weird alternate dimension. They send two D classes down there and spooky monster blah blah, until they realize the "monster" is a fairly reasonable sapient entity though distinctly not humanoid.

Elevator Pitch: It's an exploration of the Foundation's inhuman treatment of D-classes. The Eldritch entity that's down there is more concerned for the D-classes' well being than foundation personnel.

Central Narrative: Two D-classes are sent with cameras to document an extradimensional space (The Foundation at this point, knows it's unescapable, they're just curious). While wandering a mostly empty area, they stumble upon a friendly entity that appears concerned for them. The entity, while free to leave, stays to attempt to help the two get out, communicating back and forth and cooperating with the Foundation. Eventually, when the Entity finds a way to send them back with the help of the Foundation, they're rejected because it would be too costly, leaving the story ending at that.

Additional Notes: This would be a very character focused story. Though the story paints the Foundation in a bad light, I want to avoid the common tropes of the foundation being malicious idiots though, they have legitimate albeit incredibly cold reasons for their decision.
